profile.headline: Software Engineer at Leidos
profile.summary: I am a seasoned, detail-oriented, problem-solving and versatile software engineer who is fascinated with interactivity and passionate about mission-driven technical work that makes a visible positive impact.  Throughout over seven years of federal professional experience, I have developed knowledge in a large variety of programming languages, tools and frameworks, as well as the ability to get up to speed with new ones.  I am also known to be a good team player who can recognize and play to the strengths of fellow team members, as well as unhesitatingly communicate roadblocks or plans with them.

positions.title: Software Developer
positions.description: Skills: Software Development · Agile Methodologies · React.js · Web Development

company.name: Naval Surface Warfare Center Dahlgren Division

positions.title: Computer Scientist
positions.description: In this project, I independently converted automated TestCafe end-to-end tests for the mission assurance web application MADSS to JavaScript for easier readability and editing, ensuring reliability and completeness of testing coverage.  I employed careful attention to detail and repeated test runs to ensure that the intended functions of each test were not lost in translation and the tester is able to properly perform all steps of each test.

positions.title: Computer Scientist
positions.description: During this time, I joined another Agile team working on MADSS and gained firsthand experience in full-stack development.  This Agile team specialized in improving the app's irregular event report creation and management functionality.  To successfully implement new features and improvements to this part of the app, I had to work on its TypeScript frontend code, C# backend code and SQL database scripts, as well as understand and follow the flow of data between the frontend, backend and database.  Throughout my time on this team, I have become comfortable with the Agile development model, following the dataflow of full stack development, commanding attention to detail and playing to the strengths of different team members to successfully accomplish programming assignments that would conveniently assist users in creating and managing reports about potential disruptions to missions and mission resources that can help others stay informed and make responsive tactical decisions on the field.

positions.title: Computer Scientist
positions.description: In this project, I joined one of several Agile teams working on a mission assurance application to design improvements to the user interface of the app's search engine, such as support for filtering and highlighting appearances of search keywords, gaining and using new experience with Angular, Bootstrap, TypeScript, Elasticsearch and HTML/CSS to implement these features.   These improvements intend to improve the user experience in searching for data about desired items, reports, assets and missions stored within this app.

positions.title: Computer Scientist
positions.description: In this project, I used Java coding skills to independently design a heavy-duty software add-on that parses millions of articles from the Web of Science and Semantic Scholar data collections over the course of many hours to build a massive searchable inverted index of data that provides insights on modern major scientific and technological developments, as well as which countries are most prepared to leverage them.   This is my first professional use of the Java language.

positions.title: Computer Scientist
positions.description: In this position, I independently, under the direction of a supervisor, learned and used JavaScript and AngularJS to design, develop and test modules for Kibana that would enable it to visualize Elasticsearch cluster data in many beautiful and useful ways, such as Foamtree’s Voronoi treemap, with highly interactive options and filtering features, all in a painless user interface. In 2019, I delivered a concise and descriptive presentation about some of the data visualization modules I completed.

positions.title: Computer Scientist
positions.description: I was assigned on detail to briefly join an Agile team that was working on a MADIS (Marine Air Defense Integrated System) simulator, which ran on the Unity 3D engine with its backend coded in C#.  With this team, I participated in work assignments that added new improvements to the simulator and fixed outstanding bugs, such as the improvement of missile smoke trails and easier to navigate menus, which would provide a more convenient training experience to thousands of Marines using the software.  The team was also amazed at my ability to quickly learn C# and the Unity SDK in preparation for this role.

positions.title: Computer Scientist
positions.description:
In my first major project at Dahlgren, I designed an “information flow” graph creator for an earlier version of the mission assurance web application MADSS, using C#, JavaScript, HTML and/or XAML code. 
To ensure that this graph creator best helps users design helpful diagrams that properly convey information about mission-essential systems under their purview, I incorporated robust testing and knowledge of user interface principles into the graph maker's design, such as an undo/redo feature.
